12K likes, 0 comments - peterattiamd on April 1, 2025: "How do we live the longest, healthiest lives possible? 
 
It’s the question that’s driven my entire career. Over the years, I’ve developed a clear, actionable framework to help answer it.
That framework is the foundation for my free Introductory Guide to Longevity, featuring eight lessons on impactful, data-driven tactics I use with patients to improve both lifespan and healthspan.
 
And the guide is just the beginning.
You’ll also get my weekly newsletter, where I break down the latest science on longevity and health optimization in a way that makes cutting-edge research accessible and relevant. 
 
Plus, you’ll be notified about new episodes of The Drive podcast, where I explore topics like exercise, nutrition, cardiovascular health, cancer, cognition, mental well-being, and more—everything that shapes how we live and age.
The guide is free. It’s practical. And it serves as a perspective shift on how to approach the years ahead. Link in bio.".

514 likes, 21 comments - peterattiamd on October 25, 2026: "Peter’s current thoughts on rapamycin 

This clip is from “Ask Me Anything” episode # 90 (Ep. # 411) of The Drive which was released on 10/12/26.

In the full episode, we cover:

-Why Peter still considers the ketogenic diet an effective tool in the right context—but no longer for the reason he once believed
-What Peter learned after three years of regular extended fasting, how it changed his view of fasting as a longevity intervention, and who may still benefit from prolonged fasts
-How GLP-1 agonists are changing the way people lose weight, and the guardrails Peter considers essential for using them
-Why Peter is less bullish on rapamycin than he once was, and how unresolved questions around dosing have changed the way he thinks about its use in humans
-How the latest evidence on liquid biopsies has—and hasn’t—changed Peter’s thinking, and why he still considers the technology far from proven
-How Peter’s thinking on Zone 2 has evolved over the years, particularly how the amount of time someone has to train changes the way he would prescribe it
-How Peter’s thinking on squats and deadlifts has evolved, when they still make sense, and when other exercises may offer a better risk-reward tradeoff
-Much more

This AMA episode (Ep. # 411) is available exclusively for premium members. Become a member now to watch or listen on my website or your favorite podcast player.".

802 likes, 68 comments - peterattiamd on September 25, 2026: "Risks associated with thyroid supplements | Peter Attia, M.D.

This clip is from “Ask Me Anything” episode # 89 (Ep. # 308) of The Drive which was released on 9/21/26.

In the full episode, we cover:

-The two thyroid labs Peter checks on every patient, and the situations that call for a more complete workup
-The case for a lab-first approach to thyroid symptoms, and the conditions that most often masquerade as thyroid disease
-The normal range for TSH rises with age; how misreading it leads to older adults being treated when they should not be
-The problem with standard blood tests for free T3 and free T4, which are least reliable exactly when accuracy matters most, and the testing Peter requires before making a diagnosis
-How to interpret a mildly elevated TSH when everything else looks normal, and appreciating that it often resolves without treatment
-What to do when standard T4 therapy normalizes the labs but the patient still feels unwell, and how T3 is added in those cases
-Why the timing of thyroid medication deserves as much attention as the dose, given how much food and other factors reduce its absorption
-What testing revealed about the contents of popular thyroid-support supplements, and the nutrients that matter most for thyroid function
-Much more

This AMA episode (Ep. # 308) is available exclusively for premium members. Become a member now to watch or listen on my website or your favorite podcast player.".
